title: platform-scenario-fabric-and-playbook-curation-roadmap-2027
author: Rina S. Kapoor
content:
Overview
========
This roadmap describes the design, milestones, and governance for the Platform Scenario Fabric: a curated library + runtime for synthetic operational scenarios, and the associated playbook curation lifecycle. The fabric aims to make production-grade degradation, failover, capacity, and regression scenarios discoverable, executable, and repeatable for platform operators, SRE, and feature teams.

Context and motivation
----------------------
- Problem: Incident postmortems and training exercises are ad-hoc; scenarios are hard to reproduce and test across multi-tenant LLM runtime variants.
- Objective: Provide an authoritative scenario catalog ("fabric") and a lightweight orchestration layer so teams can run reproducible experiments (chaos, capacity stress, KV prefix cache failure, model-swap misfire) and link them to operator playbooks and dashboards.

Goals (top-level)
-----------------
1. Create a canonical scenario spec format and storage (v1 YAML JSON-LD) that captures intent, preconditions, expected metrics, and teardown.
2. Build a scenario execution API and a lightweight runner that can be used locally, in staging, and in the operator sandbox.
3. Integrate scenario run metadata with dashboards and alerting so runs auto-generate SLO impact reports and regression tickets.
4. Produce a curation lifecycle and governance model so playbooks remain actionable and audited.

Scope (what this roadmap covers)
--------------------------------
- Scenario spec schema and authoring UX (templates, CLI helpers)
- Scenario runner integration with existing synthetic lab and operator sandbox
- Dashboard templates and post-run SLO/regression artifacts
- Playbook association model: scenario -> runbook -> owner -> verification tests
- Training curriculum and quarterly validation cadence

Non-goals
---------
- Replacing full chaos-engine fleets (we will integrate rather than reimplement)
- Arbitrary customer-facing resiliency SLAs (this is an internal operator toolchain)

Design summary
--------------
- Scenario spec (v1 fields): id, name, intent, scope (tenant, model-variants), preconditions, run-steps (ordered), expected-observables (metrics + thresholds), rollback, tags, owner, verification-tests, artifact-links.
- Runner model: idempotent steps executed by operators or automation; supports dry-run, explain, and replay modes.
- Storage: Git-backed catalog with metadata index in the platform metadata service. Scenario change events generate audit entries.
- Telemetry hooks: each step emits structured telemetry (run_id, step_id, start/stop, samples) that feeds dashboards and a post-run synthesizer that computes SLO delta and billing impact.

Operational playbook curation process (how-to)
---------------------------------------------
1. Author: Create scenario YAML using the template. Add owner tag and at least one verification test.
2. Peer review: Submit PR to scenario-catalog repo. Two reviewers required (SRE + feature owner).
3. Lab validation: Run in the operator sandbox with dry-run, then soft-run (no customer traffic), then staged-run (small percentage synthetic traffic). Collect artifacts.
4. Playbook link: Attach or author a runbook explaining manual steps for oncall (one-pager + escalation matrix).
5. Publish: After verification, flip catalog metadata to published. Scheduled revalidation every 6 months.

Example scenario spec (YAML snippet)
-----------------------------------
# example: kv-prefix-cache-stall-2027
name: kv-prefix-cache-stall-2027
intent: "Validate operator recovery when a single kv-cache shard stalls under sustained LLM traffic"
scope: tenant: synthetic-cohort-1
preconditions:
  - model-variant: rwd-6b-quant
  - baseline-slo: p99_latency_ms <= 220
run_steps:
  - id: throttle-shard
    action: tcp-blackhole
    target: kv-cache-node-3
    duration: 300
  - id: observe
    action: monitor-metrics
    windows: [60, 300]
expected_observables:
  - name: p99_latency_ms
    threshold: "> 400"
  - name: error_rate
    threshold: "> 0.5%"
rollback:
  - action: unblackhole
  - notify: operator-team@redwood.internal

Roadmap & milestones (quarterly view)
-------------------------------------
Q1 2027
- Finalize scenario spec v1 and CLI authoring UX
- Implement Git-backed catalog and PR validation checks
- Build telemetry schema and dashboard templates (SLO delta, cost impact)

Q2 2027
- Runner v1 with dry-run and staged-run support
- Integrate with synthetic lab and operator sandbox
- Publish first 25 canonical scenarios (prefix-cache, model-swap, cold-start surge, prefetch-deadlock)

Q3 2027
- Auto-generated post-run SLO reports and regression ticket templates
- Oncall training curriculum + tabletop exercises tied to scenarios
- Add multi-tenant blast-radius simulation capabilities

Q4 2027
- Policy-driven gating (catalog scenarios used in release pipelines)
- Cross-team curation program and scenario certification badge

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Product owner: Platform Reliability (eng-platform)
- Catalog stewards: rotating pairs from Eng Platform and Eng SRE (3-month rotation)
- Release approvals: automated PR checks + human signoff by steward
- Audit: scenario-run artifacts retained for 180 days; revalidation reminders at 150 days

Success metrics (KPI)
---------------------
- Coverage: target 80% of postmortem classes mapped to canonical scenarios by EOY Q4 2027
- Reproducibility: 90% of accepted scenarios pass staged-run with documented SLO delta
- Adoption: 75% of platform SREs use the runner at least monthly for drills by Q4 2027
- Mean time to synthesize regression ticket: < 12 minutes (post-run automation)

Dashboards and alerting integration
----------------------------------
- Dashboard templates: scenario-run summary, step-level timeline, SLO delta, cost delta, artifact links
- Alerting: failed verification runs create high-priority internal tickets; post-run SLO delta > threshold opens regression alerts routed to owner_team
- Example threshold: if run SLO delta p99_latency_ms increases by > 30% and cost delta > 15%, create a regression issue automatically.

Operator training & validation cadence
-------------------------------------
- Quarterly scenario review days (platform gamespace). Each steward must vouch for 2 scenarios per quarter.
- Annual certification: read-only operators must complete 3 drills and one tabletop to be signed off.

Dependencies and risks
----------------------
- Dependencies: synthetic lab infra, telemetry ingestion SLA, scenario-catalog repo and PR automation, operator sandbox access control.
- Risks: accidental customer impact during staged runs; mitigations include strong preconditions, automated blast-radius checks, and default dry-run mode.

Appendix: minimal PR checklist for scenario acceptance
----------------------------------------------------
1. Scenario YAML validates against schema (ci)
2. Owner is set and reachable
3. At least one verification-test included
4. Runbook link present and reviewed
5. Blast-radius and tenant-scope fields are explicit
